In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work provides the first potential energy surfaces and corresponding cross sections for the C6(−)-H2 and He collisional systems, which are essential to the modeling of the C6(+) abundance in space.

the C6H- anion has been detected in the circumstellar medium around carbon-rich AGB stars, and the collisional cross-sections for this anion are needed for a more accurate modeling of their abundance in these regions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a methodology for calculating accurate PESs of van der Waals molecules, and we have used these surfaces to calculate inelastic cross sections for the C6 H(-)-H2 collisional system, the first of its kind for a molecular anion.

the C6H anion is an important species in space and its abundance is determined by the competition between the cosmic ray ionization, the dissociative recombination with electrons and the collisional excite-ation/deexcitation with the most abundant particles, He and H2.
we have provided the first ab initio PESs for a molecular anion and the first cross sections for its inelastic collisional excitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PESs and cross sections for C6H(-)+H2 are very similar to the corresponding ones for C6H+H2.
ab initio PESs for van der Waals molecules can now be obtained with high accuracy and used in collisional calculations with the most abundant molecules in the interstellar medium.

, in order to obtain reliable collisional data for molecular anions, one should use ab initio PESs that have been constructed with the best possible methods and that are accurate enough to reproduce the anisotropic features of the interaction potential.
